scenes.name: The Byrds
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Su «Mr Tambourine Man» (1965), sin pretenderlo, fue el primer gran éxito de la cultura de la droga: la voz de McGuinn, mezcla de Lennon y Dylan, en un éxtasis pasivo sobre el dron hipnótico de la Rickenbacker de doce cuerdas. Tomaron LSD con Lennon y Harrison en agosto de 1965. «Eight Miles High» (14 de marzo de 1966), empezada por Gene Clark tras su viaje a Londres y forjada en una gira escuchando a Ravi Shankar y a John Coltrane (Impressions, Africa/Brass), fundía free jazz y música india, las dos bandas sonoras secretas de beats y hipsters, en un disco nuevo e irresistible de tensión y alivio. En la rueda de prensa del 28 de marzo, con un sitar sobre la mesa que no suena en el disco, nació el «raga rock»; Crosby habló demasiado del ácido. El Gavin Report la vetó como canción de drogas y se estancó en el número 14: fue la cima de su carrera.

podcast.title: Co-founding The Flying Burrito Brothers
podcast.body: After leaving The Byrds, Chris Hillman, along with Gram Parsons, formed The Flying Burrito Brothers. He was Parsons' roommate when they wrote songs for their debut album, "Gilded Palace of Sin." "From the birds, he and Chris Hillman also formerly of the birds formed the flying burrito brothers."

podcast.title: Composing Sin City
podcast.body: Hillman woke up one morning with the opening line for "Sin City," "This old town is filled with sin, it'll swallow you in," and then woke up his roommate, Gram Parsons, who composed the melody for the song. This collaboration produced a key track on "Gilded Palace of Sin." "Some of them said he woke up one morning with this line in his head. This old town is filled with sin. It'll swallow you in. So it goes up and he wakes up his roommate, Grand Parsons, who came up with the melody for the song."

podcast.title: Discovering Emmylou Harris
podcast.body: Chris Hillman heard Emmylou Harris sing at a club outside Washington, D.C., in the early 1970s. Although he considered asking her to join The Flying Burrito Brothers (who were then without Gram Parsons), he instead recommended her to Parsons for his solo album, leading to their famous musical partnership. "Chris Hillman heard her sing at a club outside of Washington, D.C., and he considered asking her to join the flying Brito brothers who were now without Graham Parsons."
